author: Sofia Alvarez
title: University of Graz Open-Air Cinema
text:
GRAZ, Austria – The inner courtyard of the Uni-Graz main building is transforming into an atmospheric cinema hall from September 1st to 12th, 2025, screening a diverse lineup from “Top Gun: Maverick” to “Thelma & Louise” and “James Bond: No Time to Die.” This cinematic event, a collaboration with “Wanderkino” and “7th Faculty,” adds a third summer highlight to Graz’s cultural calendar, following current events at Murinsel and the now-concluded “Leslie Open.”
Graz’s Uni-Graz courtyard becomes an open-air cinema featuring classic and modern films, blending entertainment with academic insight.
The Uni-Graz campus cinema runs Sept. 1-12, 2025. Films start at 8 p.m., preceded by a scientific discussion at 7:30 p.m. Special screenings include “Conclave” with a papal election expert and “Gladiator II” with an antiquities specialist. Tickets are €5.65 and available online. The film screenings kick off at 8 p.m. nightly. Thirty minutes prior, a scientific discussion offers “opening credits,” moderated by molecular biologist Fritz Driver. Driver is also known for his nutrition expertise on the ORF program “Studio 2.”
Between Fact and Fiction, Science and Film The campus cinema explores the intersection of fact and fiction, science and film. A particular focus is placed on two specific screenings. On Monday, September 8th, the Oscar-winning film “Conclave” will be shown. Before Ralph Fiennes and Stanley Tucci grace the screen, theologian Michaela Son-Cronthaler and theologian Bernd Hillebrand will discuss the accuracy of Hollywood’s portrayal of a papal election.
On September 10th, as “Gladiator II” is set to transform the courtyard into a cinematic arena, Margit Linder from the Institute of Antiquity will offer insights. She will reveal details about the legendary sea battles held in the Colosseum and explain why Roman gladiators were less common than often believed.
“With the campus cinema, the University of Graz kicks off its Welcome Weeks, designed to welcome our new students,” stated Rector Peter Riedler. He also extended an invitation to all film enthusiasts. The courtyard can accommodate approximately 150 filmgoers. In case of inclement weather, the screenings will be moved to the university’s auditorium. Tickets are priced at €5.65 per evening and can be purchased in advance online.
Summer’s End at Leslie Open and Murinsel As for the other summer events in Graz, the “Leslie Open” in the Joanneumviertel concludes on August 30th. The final showings include the “Diagonal” audience award-winning film “Perla” today at 8 p.m., the Colombian drama “Monos – Between Heaven and Hell” on Friday at 8 p.m., and the highly anticipated film “Sirât” on Saturday at 8 p.m.
At Murinsel, the US music comedy “Pitch Perfect” is scheduled for next Monday. Tuesday features a contrasting program with David Lynch’s cult film “The Elephant Man,” followed by the 1960s comedy classic “The Party Schreck” on Wednesday. The Murinsel events will wrap up on Monday, September 8th, with the British coming-of-age drama “Billy Elliot,” with all films starting at 8 p.m.
